correctness.rationale: For each nonconstant palindrome abcba, the event is the ordered appearance of edges abcb and bcba in a cyclic Euler tour. Contracting their consecutive use yields a tagged edge in a balanced digraph and a bijection of Euler tours. BEST computes its probability by the ratio of directed spanning-tree cofactors divided by q-1. The Laplacian update is rank one, with exact group inverse L#=(I+P+P²-3J)/q because P³=J. Evaluating the bilinear form gives all four equality-pattern fractions, and summing all ordered triples yields E X=q²-2-2/q. Constant patterns cannot occur. Every step handles q=2 and parallel/loop contracted edges. A separate Python checker exhaustively enumerated all 16 binary order-four cycles and independently computed q=2,3 spanning-tree cofactors; all checked cases agree. No finite computation substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The quantitative law gives individual palindrome-pattern probabilities and a uniform-cycle mean for an exact motif/order combination; the closest inspected reverse-coverage publications address palindrome counts or graph constraints in different covering ensembles, while generalized-de-Bruijn and BWT work gives no dominating event-probability theorem. Existing BEST and matrix-tree facts are explicit premises, not claimed as discoveries. Remaining priority risk concerns inaccessible earlier chapter text and unindexed/general Euler-tour applications.
residual_risks: The 2018 RECOMB chapter full body was inaccessible; its 2020 journal extension was compared using the available technical text, but journal/preprint versions can differ.
A closed-form implication hidden in unindexed literature or a different Euler-tour counting language could cover the new statement; absence from targeted searches is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Five-letter palindromic motifs are the first natural reversal-symmetric factors beyond the forced four-mer content of an order-four de Bruijn cycle. Their frequency varies even in the binary case. The finding resolves the uniform exact expectation for every alphabet size and, more strongly, every possible equality type of a particular palindrome. The combinatorial value lies in translating local motifs into a nontrivial tagged-edge contraction and explicit low-step Markov-chain Green function, yielding exact all-alphabet rational laws. This is a motivated structural local-pattern statistic, not a normalization check or one isolated small computation.
